context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at 3,000 TPS within a sub-50ms P99 latency window and manages suspicious cases for human analysts. Operating under strict PCI-DSS Level 1 constraints, it ensures tamper-evident auditability and zero-downtime model updates.

## Key Elements
- **Merchant Integration Systems**: External clients submitting payment authorizations via gRPC/HTTPS.
- **Fraud Analysts**: Internal users reviewing flagged transactions via TLS.
- **Identity Provider**: External OIDC/IAM service for analyst Single Sign-On.
- **API Gateway / Network Load Balancer (NLB)**: AWS managed ingress terminating TLS and routing traffic.
- **Scoring Engine**: Containerized microservice processing real-time fraud scoring using cached rule sets.
- **Case Management Portal**: Web interface for analysts to investigate flagged transactions.
- **Audit Storage**: AWS S3 with Object Lock and KMS encryption for tamper-evident 7-year retention.

## Relationships
- **Merchant Systems to NLB**: Push payment authorizations via gRPC/HTTPS with mandatory mTLS and OAuth2/JWT validation.
- **Fraud Analysts to Case Management Portal**: Access review queues over TLS authenticated via OIDC.
- **Scoring Engine to Audit Storage**: Stream cryptographic hash-chained decision logs and inputs via AWS PrivateLink.
- **Scoring Engine to Tokenization Proxy**: Process ephemeral payment payloads to mask Primary Account Numbers (PAN).

## Technology Stack
- **AWS eu-west-1**: Target cloud provider delivering multi-AZ redundancy within a €25,000 monthly budget.
- **Amazon ECS/EKS on Graviton Instances**: Container orchestration utilizing cost-effective ARM-based processors for high-throughput scoring and case management.
- **Terraform**: Infrastructure-as-Code tool automating GitOps-driven zero-downtime deployments.
- **AWS KMS & S3 Object Lock**: Encryption and WORM storage ensuring PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year tamper-evident audit trails.
- **OpenTelemetry & Prometheus/Grafana**: Distributed tracing and metrics collection monitoring P99 latency.

## Rationale
The architecture prioritizes sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS by employing stateless scoring containers, AWS Graviton instances, and cached rule sets within a single AWS region. It strictly fulfills PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit mandates using cryptographic signing, AWS KMS encryption, and WORM-compliant S3 storage while remaining operable by a three-engineer team under a €25,000 monthly budget.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at 3,000 TPS within a sub-50ms P99 latency SLA. It provides a secure case management portal for fraud analysts while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year tamper-evident audit trail.

## Key Elements
- Merchants and API Gateway / Network Load Balancer (NLB)
- Fraud Analysts and Identity Provider
- Scoring Engine Container (Go, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Portal Container (Node.js/TypeScript, PostgreSQL)
- Audit Storage & Processing (Amazon SQS, Amazon Kinesis Firehose, S3 Object Lock)
- Feature Store (Redis Cluster)

## Relationships
- Merchant Integration Systems to API Gateway via HTTPS (REST/JSON)
- API Gateway to Scoring Engine via gRPC over HTTP/2
- Scoring Engine to Redis Cluster via TCP (In-memory feature lookups)
- Scoring Engine to Amazon SQS via AWS SDK (Async audit events)
- Case Management Portal to PostgreSQL via TLS
- Kinesis Firehose to S3 Object Lock via HTTPS (WORM audit storage)

## Technology Stack
- **Compute:** AWS ECS Fargate for container orchestration with Go (Scoring Engine) and Node.js/TypeScript (Case Management Portal) for optimal performance and memory safety.
- **Data & Caching:** Redis Cluster for low-latency feature lookups; PostgreSQL for relational case management persistence.
- **Messaging & Streaming:** Amazon SQS for asynchronous event decoupling; Amazon Kinesis Firehose for ingestion into storage.
- **Storage & Compliance:** Amazon S3 with S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for 7-year tamper-evident audit retention.
- **Security & Networking:** mTLS for inter-container communication, OAuth2/OIDC for Identity Provider integration, AWS Cloud Map for internal service discovery.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples the high-throughput real-time payment path from analytical case management to protect the sub-50ms SLA and strict security boundaries. Standardizing on managed AWS services enables a three-engineer team to operate the platform reliably within the €25,000 monthly budget while satisfying PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit requirements.

Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Scoring Engine is a real-time payment fraud screening container that evaluates card-not-present transactions for a mid-size payment processor. It provides sub-50ms P99 latency decisions (approve, decline, review) while maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year auditability mandate.

## Key Elements
- Scoring Engine Container (Go, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Request Handler Component (Go, gRPC)
- Model Evaluator Component (ONNX Runtime, Dual-Buffer Registry)
- Feature Aggregator Component (Concurrent Redis Pipeline)
- Audit Dispatcher Component (Amazon SQS, AWS SDK)
- Redis Cluster (Feature Store)
- Amazon SQS & S3 (Audit Queue and Storage)

## Relationships
- API Gateway / Network Load Balancer (NLB) -> Scoring Engine: Route payment evaluation requests [gRPC over HTTP/2, mTLS]
- Scoring Engine -> Redis Cluster: Perform in-memory feature lookups [TCP, TLS 1.3]
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS: Emit asynchronous, KMS-signed audit events [AWS SDK, HTTPS]
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon S3: Persist tamper-evident audit logs [Amazon Kinesis Firehose]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for high-throughput concurrency and minimal garbage collection overhead to satisfy sub-50ms P99 latency.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration matching the 25,000 EUR monthly budget without idle server management.
- Redis Cluster: In-memory cache providing sub-15ms feature aggregation and velocity checks.
- ONNX Runtime: Embedded machine learning execution engine enabling zero-downtime model hot-swapping via atomic pointer swaps.
- Amazon SQS & S3 with S3 Object Lock: Guarantees tamper-evident, 7-year regulatory audit retention.

## Rationale
This architecture balances ultra-low latency processing at 3,000 TPS with strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security and tamper-evident auditability. Decoupling real-time scoring from asynchronous auditing ensures the system meets its availability and performance constraints within the fixed infrastructure budget.

Case Management Portal.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Portal provides fraud analysts with an investigative interface to review suspicious payment transactions flagged by the real-time scoring engine. It ensures rapid triage and compliance with strict regulatory frameworks while protecting sensitive cardholder data.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts
- React Web UI (TypeScript)
- NestJS API Controller
- Case Service (TypeScript)
- Prisma ORM (Data Access Layer)
- Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
- External Identity Provider
- Audit Storage (Amazon S3 with S3 Object Lock)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analysts -> React Web UI: Investigate flagged transactions and manage cases [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- React Web UI -> NestJS API Controller: Invoke REST endpoints and fetch investigation data [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- NestJS API Controller -> Case Service: Execute business logic for case resolution [In-memory]
- Case Service -> Prisma ORM: Query and persist case metadata [Internal]
- Prisma ORM -> Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL: Persist relational case data [TCP/SSL, TLS 1.3, IAM authentication]
- NestJS API Controller -> External Identity Provider: Authenticate users and validate tokens [OIDC/JWT]
- NestJS API Controller -> Audit Storage: Retrieve historical decision explanations [Secure REST]

## Technology Stack
- React, TypeScript: Powers the analyst web UI for rapid, responsive case triage.
- NestJS, TypeScript: Provides a structured, scalable REST API controller architecture.
- Prisma ORM: Manages type-safe database access and parameterized queries to prevent injection vectors.
- Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL: Stores relational case data securely with automated Multi-AZ failover and AWS KMS encryption at rest.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Runs containerized services without manual server provisioning to fit the 3-engineer team constraint.

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security and 7-year auditability requirements with a cost-effective, easily maintainable serverless cloud footprint. By utilizing managed AWS services, isolated private subnets, and strict data masking, it protects cardholder data while empowering a small engineering team to operate within budget.

Feature Store.analysis:
## Overview
[The Feature Store component provides low-latency behavioral feature lookups to power real-time fraud scoring for payment authorizations. It ensures rapid model iteration without downtime while maintaining strict PCI-DSS compliance and operational efficiency.]

## Key Elements
- Feature Store (AWS ElastiCache Redis Cluster)
- Feature Ingestion Worker (Python, Celery)
- Point-in-Time Retrieval API (Embedded Redis modules)
- Data Synchronization Service
- Schema Registry Component
- TTL Management Module

## Relationships
- Scoring Engine -> Feature Store: Performs in-memory feature lookups [TCP, Redis RESP, TLS]
- Feature Ingestion Worker -> Feature Store: Ingests real-time transaction streams and updates behavioral aggregates [TCP, Redis RESP]
- Data Synchronization Service -> Amazon S3: Manages asynchronous persistence for audit retention [HTTPS, AWS KMS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ElastiCache for Redis: In-memory storage providing sub-millisecond feature retrieval to meet the 50ms latency SLA
- Python / Celery: Ingestion worker technology for processing real-time transaction streams and rolling aggregates
- AWS KMS: Manages encryption keys at rest for data protection and compliance
- Terraform: Infrastructure-as-code tool for managing cluster deployment within budget constraints

## Rationale
[This architecture utilizes an in-memory Redis cluster to guarantee sub-millisecond feature retrieval, ensuring the scoring engine meets its strict P99 latency threshold. Automated failover, strict memory TTLs, and encryption mechanisms satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 25,000 EUR monthly budget constraint while supporting a small engineering team.]

Audit Queue.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and manage manual analyst reviews. The architecture guarantees PCI-DSS compliance, 7-year auditability, and sub-50ms decision latency within a fixed infrastructure budget.

## Key Elements
- Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate, Go)
- Audit Queue (Amazon SQS Standard/FIFO with DLQ)
- Audit Stream Processor (Amazon Kinesis Firehose)
- Audit Storage (Amazon S3 with S3 Object Lock)
- Feature Store (Redis Cluster)
- Case Management Portal (Node.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL)
- Fraud Analysts

## Relationships
- Scoring Engine -> Audit Queue: Enqueue audit payload [HTTPS / AWS SDK with SigV4]
- Scoring Engine -> Feature Store: Read/Write features [Redis Protocol]
- Audit Queue -> Audit Stream Processor: Deliver audit batch [HTTPS Long Polling]
- Audit Stream Processor -> Audit Storage: Flush tamper-evident logs [S3 API]
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management Portal: Review flagged transactions [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration for cost efficiency and minimal operational overhead
- Amazon SQS: Asynchronous message queuing to decouple scoring from storage and prevent latency
- Amazon S3 with S3 Object Lock: WORM-compliant storage ensuring 7-year immutable audit logs
- Redis Cluster: Low-latency in-memory feature storage to satisfy the 50ms P99 SLA
- AWS KMS: Customer-managed keys enforcing encryption at rest for PCI-DSS compliance

## Rationale
Managed AWS services minimize operational burden, fitting the three-engineer team constraint and 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Asynchronous decoupling via SQS protects critical payment latency while ensuring 100% audit capture.

Audit Stream Processor.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that processes card-not-present authorizations for a mid-size payment processor. Its core purpose is to score transactions for fraud, manage suspicious cases, and maintain secure, auditable records.]

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts
- Merchant Integration Systems
- Identity Provider
- API Gateway / Network Load Balancer (NLB)
- Scoring Engine (Go, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Portal (Node.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL)
- Feature Store (Redis Cluster)
- Audit Queue (Amazon SQS)
- Audit Stream Processor (Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose)
- Audit Storage (Amazon S3, S3 Object Lock)

## Relationships
- Merchant Integration Systems -> API Gateway / Network Load Balancer: Submit payment authorizations [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- API Gateway / Network Load Balancer -> Scoring Engine: Route authorization requests [gRPC / HTTPS]
- Scoring Engine -> Feature Store: Fetch user features and model weights [Redis Protocol]
- Scoring Engine -> Case Management Portal: Forward suspicious transactions for analyst review [REST / HTTPS]
- Scoring Engine -> Audit Queue: Publish decision inputs, model versions, and explanations [Amazon SQS API / HTTPS]
- Audit Queue -> Audit Stream Processor: Ingest raw decision payloads [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Audit Stream Processor -> Audit Storage: Write immutable audit records for WORM storage [HTTPS / S3 API]

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Provider: AWS (Region: eu-west-1) for scalable, compliant infrastructure within budget constraints
- Container Runtime: AWS ECS Fargate for lightweight, serverless container orchestration
- Core Services: Go for high-performance scoring and Node.js with TypeScript for case management
- Data Storage: PostgreSQL for case management, Redis Cluster for low-latency feature lookups, and Amazon S3 with S3 Object Lock for tamper-evident audit storage
- Streaming & Security: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with AWS KMS encryption and TLS 1.3 for secure audit pipelines

## Rationale
[This architecture satisfies PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year audit requirement while adhering to a strict 25,000 EUR monthly budget and operating constraints of a 3-engineer team. Serverless and managed AWS components minimize operational overhead while guaranteeing sub-50ms P99 latency and high availability.]

Audit Storage.analysis:
## Overview
[Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening screens card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor and enables fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions. It ensures sub-50ms P99 decision latency while maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year audit retention within a 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget.]

## Key Elements
- External Users: Fraud Analysts, Merchant Integration Systems
- External Services: Identity Provider
- Infrastructure: API Gateway / Network Load Balancer (NLB)
- Core Containers: Scoring Engine, Case Management Portal, Feature Store, Audit Queue, Audit Stream Processor, Audit Storage
- Audit Storage Components: Amazon S3, S3 Object Lock, AWS KMS, AWS VPC Gateway Endpoints

## Relationships
- Merchant Integration Systems -> API Gateway / NLB: Submit payment authorization requests [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- API Gateway / NLB -> Scoring Engine: Route authorization requests [gRPC / REST]
- Scoring Engine <-> Feature Store: Fetch user and transaction features [Redis Cluster Protocol / RESP]
- Scoring Engine -> Audit Queue: Publish decision events asynchronously [Amazon SQS]
- Audit Queue -> Audit Stream Processor: Stream decision payloads [Amazon Kinesis Firehose]
- Audit Stream Processor -> Audit Storage: Write immutable audit records [HTTPS / S3 PutObject]
- Case Management Portal <-> Scoring Engine: Fetch case details and update rules [REST / HTTPS]
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management Portal: Review flagged payments [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Provider: AWS (Region: eu-west-1) for managed scalability and compliance tooling
- Compute: AWS ECS Fargate for containerized scoring execution
- Backend & Datastores: Node.js/TypeScript and PostgreSQL for Case Management; Redis Cluster for ultra-low latency feature storage
- Audit & Compliance: Amazon S3 with Object Lock in Compliance Mode for WORM-compliant 7-year tamper-evident retention
- Security & Encryption: AWS KMS Customer Managed Keys (CMKs) for data at rest; TLS 1.3 enforced via bucket policies for data in transit; AWS VPC Gateway Endpoints for network isolation

## Rationale
[This AWS-native serverless and managed container architecture meets the strict 50ms P99 latency and 7-year tamper-evident audit requirements by leveraging in-memory Redis caching and immutable S3 Object Lock storage. Furthermore, it operates within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget and supports operation by a lean three-engineer team through fully managed services.]
